issues.title: [BugFix][Multimodal] Select worst-case DeepSeek-V4 VL dummy images
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #20106.

Ports [vllm-project/vllm#59373](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59373) to Ascend's local DeepSeek-V4 VL preprocessing implementation. Although the upstream fix is included in vLLM v0.32.0, Ascend registers its own processing classes and needs the corresponding change.

The previous selector assumed that a square image maximized the vision workload within the token budget. Each aligner row consumes an additional `IMAGE_NEW_LINE` token, so a wider image can produce more ViT patches and placeholder tokens. The square dummy can underestimate multimodal profiling memory and leave an overly optimistic KV cache budget.

The updated selector searches feasible LLM grids, respects `vision_max_wh_ratio`, and maximizes the ViT patch count, breaking ties by sentinel token count. It preserves headroom for position-dependent compressor padding.

With the default configuration:

| Dummy image | Dimensions (width x height) | ViT patches | Placeholder tokens, excluding leading compressor padding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Previous | 756 x 756 | 2,916 | 346 |
| Updated | 1,932 x 336 | 3,312 | 378 |

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DeepSeek-V4 VL profiling uses a more representative worst-case dummy image. This may increase profiled multimodal memory and consequently reduce the automatically allocated KV cache capacity. The NPU vision-component measurements below support the square-input memory underestimate; the effect on full-model profiling and the resulting KV cache budget remains unverified.

Added the bugfix release note fragment `release_notes/fragments/20107.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

**Local CPU validation**

Executed with vLLM v0.32.0+cpu using the repository's standard unit-test setup, including its NPU mocks:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_vision_preprocess.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_vision.py
```

Result: **21 passed** locally. Rerunning the same two CPU UT files in the NPU test container also gave **21 passed**. These mocked CPU UTs are counted separately from the real NPU component execution below.

The 14 added parametrized cases cover:

- The wide-image regression and actual processor patch/token counts.
- Aspect-ratio limits of `1`, `2`, `8`, and `None`, including verification that preprocessing preserves the selected dimensions.
- Token budgets of `384` and `385` across all four compressor-padding offsets.
- Dummy-input generation and preprocessing for two images.

Restoring only the original selector in the test process made both focused regression tests fail as expected: `test_dummy_image_covers_wide_image` and `test_dummy_builder_uses_worst_case_images`. The linked issue includes a standalone processor-level reproduction.

**Repository checks**

```bash
bash format.sh ci
git diff --check
```

Both passed locally. Local pytest execution covered the two files listed above; broader CPU coverage is provided by PR CI.

**PR CPU CI (recorded results for head `7214b50b1dc758276956ffb8fb0da1f986537171`)**

| vLLM dependency | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v0.32.0 | **13,053 passed, 91 skipped** | [Release CPU UT](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/40656729488/job/122712834907) |
| Pinned upstream main `544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542` | **13,063 passed, 81 skipped** | [Main CPU UT](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/40656729488/job/122712834892) |

Pre-commit, DCO, and both English and Chinese documentation builds also passed.

In the linked CI run, `ci-gate` failed because no test-enabling label (`ready-precise`, `ready-all`, or `main2main`) was set, so the selected-test jobs were skipped. This was a test-admission gate rather than a failed CPU UT assertion; the CPU results above do not imply that all CI checks passed. [Gate log](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/40656729488/job/122718263055)

**Real NPU vision-component validation**

Tested PR head `7214b50b1dc758276956ffb8fb0da1f986537171` on Ascend A3 with vLLM 0.32.0+empty, torch 2.10.0+cpu, torch-npu 2.10.0.post7, and CANN 9.2.0.

Manual procedure: load the real `vision.*` and `aligner.*` weights from the `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp` checkpoint (263 tensors; complete 32-layer ViT + aligner; BF16). Preprocess images with the local image processor, then call the existing `_process_image_input()` method in a vision-only harness. Validate output count, shape, NPU device, dtype, and finite values. The language backbone was not constructed.

| Workload | Component calls | NPU ViT forwards |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Square reference (756 x 756) and updated dummy (1932 x 336), one each | 2 | 2 |
| Normal single-image inputs (756 x 756) | 3 | 3 |
| Wide single-image inputs (1932 x 336) | 3 | 3 |
| Two wide images per call | 3 | 6 |
| A new normal image after each two-image call | 3 | 3 |
| **Total** | **14** | **17** |

All **14 component calls / 17 NPU ViT forwards passed**. Each normal image produced `[324, 4096]`; each wide image produced `[368, 4096]`, and two-image calls returned two outputs. Outputs had the expected device/dtype and no NaN/Inf. The updated dummy produced **3312 patches / 378 placeholder tokens** (excluding leading compressor padding), matching the tested legal wide image.

**Component memory observations**

Synchronize the NPU and reset peak-memory statistics before each call; read `torch.npu.max_memory_allocated()` after the forward completes. This measures the test process's PyTorch NPU allocator peak, including the vision-component weights and forward allocations.

| Input | Peak allocated NPU memory |
| --- | ---: |
| Square reference / normal image | 2197.08 MiB |
| Updated dummy / legal wide image | 2544.60 MiB |
| Two wide images, processed sequentially | 2554.67 MiB |

The three normal-image runs and three wide-image runs reproduced their respective peaks. The wide-image peak was **347.52 MiB higher**, supporting the original square dummy's underestimate of vision-component memory. These measurements compare input shapes within the same component; they are not paired baseline/fixed full-service runs and cannot be converted directly into a KV cache budget change.

**Remaining validation**

Full-model startup and Worker memory profiling did not complete because of test-environment compatibility limitations; **no HTTP end-to-end requests were executed**. Full-service wide-/multi-image inference, the resulting KV cache budget, and an end-to-end OOM reproduction remain unverified. Component success does not establish an end-to-end OOM fix or full-service accuracy/performance.

**AI assistance**

OpenAI Codex assisted with the upstream port, regression tests, CPU and NPU component validation, and PR preparation. The validation results and outstanding hardware checks are documented above.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change involves
  boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max values,
  off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable, I
  added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or `tests/e2e/`.
- [x] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths (exceptions,
  timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

No new exception-handling paths are introduced. Component-level NPU memory measurements are reported above; full-service profiling and performance validation remain outstanding.

issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR makes Model Runner V2 the default on Ascend when `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` is unset. The old architecture, feature, platform, and Triton whitelist is replaced by a blacklist in `vllm_ascend/mrv2_utils.py`.

When the env var is unset, a request uses V2 unless it matches one of these V1 fallbacks:

**Models / platform**

- Hy3-preview (`HYV3*`)
- Gemma4 (`Gemma4*`)
- 310P
- encoder-decoder (Whisper)
- pooling KV

**Features**

- LoRA
- VL encoder disaggregation (`ec_transfer_config` / encoder-only)
- `draft_window_size`
- suffix speculative decoding
- ngram / `ngram_gpu`
- `parallel_drafting`
- dflash2 graph (DFlash2 without `enforce_eager`)

An explicit override still wins:

- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` forces V1
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` forces V2

Upstream GPU / Triton V2 validation does not apply; Ascend owns runner selection.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Unset `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` now defaults to Model Runner V2, except for the blacklist above. Keep V1 with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`. Explicit `0` / `1` is unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests: `tests/ut/test_mrv2_utils.py` (default V2, blacklist fallback, env override)
- E2E / nightly: default V2 path, plus a few explicit `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` pins
- CI: cpu-ut / e2e on this PR


- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607

Disabling MegaMoe on the exact same build/environment produces correct output — so the problem is isolated to the MegaMoe path. **Important note**: MegaMoe enablement for Kimi K3 was **cherry-picked** as commit `5a9de6576` ("feat(moe): enable MegaMoe for Kimi K3") on top of the v0.27.1rc nightly (`67dd25526`). We are not sure whether the issue is introduced by the picked changes or by the interaction between the picked code and the CANN weekly ops package — the full diff of the pick is attached below. ## Environment - Hardware: Atlas 800I A3 (910_93), 8 nodes x 16 NPU - Deployment: **PD-disaggregated 4P4D**, both sides DP4/TP16 + DCP16, MooncakeConnectorV1 KV transfer, dspark speculative decoding issues.title: [Feature] Support native GLM PCP prefill to RecoverSSM decode transfer
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable a native GLM KDA prefill producer with PCP to hand committed state to a RecoverSSM decode consumer through MooncakeConnectorV2. The connector advertises head ownership, maps TP/PCP owners, transfers convolution/recurrent slices with independent page strides, and excludes D-local verify records. It reuses upstream SSM convolution geometry and adds no packing kernel or Triton arithmetic.

The PCP layer invocation reads request metadata inside an opaque custom op so metadata-free warmup cannot freeze gather/restore branches. The change also pads sparse-index selections to match PCP query capacity without modifying actual selections, recognizes UniformType Mamba groups, avoids verifying unproposed placeholders on D's first forward, and feeds the known prompt tail into P's final MTP prefill KV entry.

Related upstream implementations:

1. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37635 introduces heterogeneous-TP three-read convolution-state geometry. This PR reuses the upstream `MambaConvSplitInfo` helper for Mooncake GLM state slices.
2. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37310 establishes the N-1 prefill handoff for stateful P/D separation. The remaining prompt token is executed on D; this PR fixes the MTP bootstrap around that boundary.
3. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41869 extends NIXL P/D to GDN. It is related backend-specific state-transfer work; this PR adapts GLM native/RecoverSSM state through Mooncake and does not claim NIXL validation.

Ascend dependencies already on main:

1. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20128 supplies the existing RecoverSSM Triton operators; their arithmetic is unchanged here.
2. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20131 supplies GLM RecoverSSM MRV2/framework integration.
3. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20369 supplies prefix-cache alignment. Its implementation and tests were removed from this PR diff after rebasing; this PR does not reintroduce that feature.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. It adds experimental native-P/RecoverSSM-D handoff with PCP and differing TP/head ownership. Peers must agree on weights, state dtypes/layout, speculative window, cache mode and effective state block size. D retains PP1/PCP1. The transfer contract also covers pure-DP D (TP1/DP8 with EP8) and multiple native producer instances; validation status is tracked in the experiment comment. No new environment variable is introduced. Release note: release_notes/fragments/20453.yaml.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit coverage includes global head/byte-coordinate references, invalid contracts, metadata serialization, request bootstrap lifecycle, and one compiled graph switching warmup/prefill/decode contexts. Operator-boundary documentation is in vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/glm5next_kda_pcp_layer.md.

Experimental configurations, measured results, known failures, source revisions and outstanding checks are maintained in [the experiment comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20453#issuecomment-6541117335). Historical measurements are explicitly separated from rebased-source validation. The PR remains a draft while the model accuracy non-regression gate and outstanding reference/performance checks remain open.

issues.title: [Performance] Fuse DSA V4.1 slot-mapping 2D/flat computation into one Triton kernel
issues.body:
## What this PR does / why we need it?

The DSA V4.1 attention-metadata builder launches per-KV-cache-group slot-mapping 2D/flat computation as ~13 eager aclnn operators (GeScalar, ClampMin, DivMods, Remainder, SWhere, ViewCopy) every step. This change fuses those device operations into one Triton kernel (compute_slot_mapping_2d) that computes validity, block/offset division, selection and the three buffer writes in a single launch, reusing the existing persistent buffers. Metadata preparation remains outside model graphs.

The fused kernel runs for both prefill and decode forwards (the metadata build executes on every forward step), so host-side launch overhead is cut across the whole serving path. It handles the non-compressed & ratio==2 cache groups; the compressed ratio==2 masking path (valid_end / positions / ring state) keeps the eager implementation, as does the A5 packed-cache path. On CPU / unit tests the build falls back to the original eager PyTorch chain (Triton kernels cannot launch on CPU tensors).

The output is bit-identical to the original eager chain (verified), and there are no new configuration flags, model-name checks or device-to-host synchronizations.

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Lower attention-metadata preparation overhead for DSA V4.1 prefill/decode forwards. Release note: release_notes/fragments/20291.yaml.

## How was this patch tested?

Operator correctness — fused vs. unfused

Element-wise equivalence of the kernel logic vs. the original eager chain: 4,500 random cases (block_size {128,64,256} × compressed {true,false} × ratio {1,2}), 100% exact match (rtol=0, atol=0).
CPU unit tests: the CPU fallback path keeps CPU tensors on the eager chain; cpu-ut passes.
NPU verification: compute_slot_mapping_2d output vs. the eager chain compared element-wise on device.

End-to-end performance — Ascend 910B, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash w8a8, both runs on v0.30.0rc2, 32 cards (2 Prefill: DP2TP8 + 2 Decode: DP8TP2), 3k/1k tokens, concurrency ~113 (max 128), 512 requests, 0 failures:

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 3.20 | 3.46 | +8.0% |
| Output token throughput (token/s) | 3277.6 | 3539.4 | +8.0% |
| Avg end-to-end latency (ms) | 35366 | 32870 | -7.1% |
| Benchmark duration (ms) | 159959 | 148130 | -7.4% |
| Time per output token (TPOT, ms) | 31.0 | 28.6 | -7.7% |
| Time to first token (TTFT, ms) | 3608.3 | 3648.7 | +1.1% |

TTFT rose slightly (+1.1%), which is outside the scope of this metadata-build optimization and reflects prefill/queueing variance.

issues.title: [Performance] Consume strided BA inputs directly in GDN gating
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

GDN splits the BA projection into views and copies each to contiguous storage before gating. Pass independent row/head strides to the existing Triton kernel and remove the two materializations at the producer.

The input addressing supports row gaps, column strides, transposed and expanded inputs, while outputs remain contiguous. Keep the existing math, precision, grid and tiling. Dense inputs retain the original flat addressing; unit-head-stride views use simplified addresses and other layouts use independent row/head strides. Only layout categories are constexpr; raw strides and token counts remain dynamic, with no batch threshold. A2/A3/A5 use this shared Triton wrapper; the separate 310P path is unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Removed BA projection copies before GDN gating by allowing the Triton kernel to read the original input strides. No configuration or checkpoint format change. The layout fix is now integrated. issues.title: [Performance][Attention] Fuse SFA K-path ops and enable PROLOG_V3 fused decode for non-PD serving
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

GLM5.2 SFA profiling shows several removable ops in the K processing path of every layer. This PR removes them and makes PROLOG_V3 the default fused preprocessing for quantized SFA layers in every deployment:

1. **Per-step int64 slot cast**: `exec_kv` re-cast the shared slot mapping to int64 for `npu_kv_rmsnorm_rope_cache` in every layer, although all layers of a scheduling step receive the same int32 slot tensor. The conversion is now cached on the attention metadata (`_int64_kv_slots`), so one Cast kernel runs per step instead of one per layer (~5us x num_layers per step). The PROLOG_V3 fused preprocess reuses the same cached conversion for its int64 cache indices.

2. **Duplicate indexer GEMM**: the indexer's k path (`forward_k`) and top-k stage (`forward`) both ran the same `wk_weights_proj` GEMM (`[tokens, hidden] x [160, hidden]`) on the same hidden states, once for the indexer K and once for the lightning-indexer weights. `forward_k` now returns the non-K tail of the GEMM output and `forward` reuses it, removing one GEMM plus its slice copy per indexer layer per step (falling back to the GEMM only when the two stages are handed different tensors).

3. **Redundant `.contiguous()` copies**: `npu_rms_norm` returns a contiguous tensor so the copy before the C8 block-quant view was discarded, and `torch.cat` already allocates contiguous outputs for the sparse-attention query concat.

4. **PROLOG_V3 by default, no new switch**: PROLOG_V3 (the `npu_mla_prolog_v3` single fused op covering qkv proj + norm + rope + q up-proj + C8 quantize/pack + direct cache write) was previously gated on `is_kv_consumer`, i.e. only PD-disaggregated decode workers could take it. It is now the default fused preprocessing for quantized SFA layers in every deployment (plain serving, PD KV producers and KV consumers) and serves every attention state: prefill and decode steps both take the fused path (the per-step attention-state fallback to NATIVE is gone; only MLAPO keeps its token-count limit). Switch convergence:
   - `enable_dsa_cp` is the prefill/P-node route selector: it routes to `AscendSFADSACPImpl`, which unconditionally disables fused preprocessing, so the two are mutually exclusive by construction (dsa_cp on => prolog off, dsa_cp off => prolog on);
   - the C8 switches (`enable_sparse_sfa_c8` / `enable_sparse_li_c8`) only select the KV cache layout and are orthogonal to this choice; W8A8Dynamic layers no longer require `enable_sparse_sfa_c8` to take the fused path;
   - unquantized layers keep the NATIVE chain outside KV consumers because the unquantized weight preparation transposes `fused_qkv_a_proj.weight` in place, which the NATIVE fallback still consumes;
   - `dispose_layer` stays gated on `is_kv_consumer` so producers and plain-serving workers keep the fallback weights (the cost is the extra PROLOG_V3 weight copies: memory, not correctness).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, a default behavior change: quantized (W8A8Dynamic / W8A8MXFP8) SFA deployments now take the PROLOG_V3 fused preprocessing for both prefill and decode steps by default, without any additional-config option. Deployments on `enable_dsa_cp` (prefill/P-node CP route) and unquantized (bf16) layers are unaffected. The default trades extra NPU weight memory (the retained qkv_a/q_b fallback weights on producers and plain-serving workers) for kernel savings.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests added/updated in `tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_v1.py`:
  - per-step int64 slot caching (passthrough / convert-and-cache / re-convert on new step) and `exec_kv` reusing the cached slots across layers;
  - single `wk_weights_proj` invocation across the indexer k path and top-k stage (plus the fallback recomputation when the tensors differ);
  - PROLOG_V3 routing matrix for the default gate (non-PD W8A8Dynamic with and without C8 -> PROLOG_V3; non-PD MXFP8 -> PROLOG_V3; non-PD unquantized -> NATIVE; KV producer quantized -> PROLOG_V3, unquantized -> NATIVE);
  - weight-disposal guard confirming non-consumer workers keep the fallback weights.

- `uvx ruff==0.14.0 check` and `format --check` on all touched Python files.
- CI cpu-ut green (4431+ tests).

**End-to-end A/B benchmark: DSA-CP route (main) vs PROLOG_V3 route (this PR)** (Atlas 800 A3, 16x 910B, CANN 9.1.0, vllm 0.28.0, GLM-5.2-w4a8c8, DP2xTP8 + EP):

The comparison is between the two decode preprocessing routes, each in its best usable configuration. `enable_dsa_cp` requires SP-MoE and unconditionally disables the fused preprocessing path, so the two options are mutually exclusive by construction; everything else is identical on both sides:

| item | base (main `125924bb2`) | PR (`cb525a869`) |
|---|---|---|
| **decode preprocessing route** | `enable_dsa_cp=true` | PROLOG_V3 route (now the default; measured with the earlier opt-in build of this PR) |

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add DeepSeek V4.1 framework support on top of the native operators introduced in #16422, porting the framework integration from #16423 and adapting it to main.

- Register the V4.1 text and vision models and integrate model configuration, weight loading, ModelSlim quantization, and frontend encoding/reasoning/tool-call handling.
- Add V4.1 DSA attention and context parallelism, compressed/shared KV cache allocation, ring-buffer state, and DSpark integration while preserving main's model-runner and padded-page cache behavior.
- Support Engram HBM storage and optional host offload. Host offload keeps tables on CPU and stages selected BF16 rows through bounded pinned buffers, with a fused INT8 CPU lookup operator and fixed-address graph inputs.
- Add regression coverage, the model tutorial, and A3 launch examples. Fix fresh-process model import ordering and the API-node/headless DP launch arguments.

The branch contains two commits: framework integration (`4e07c7f`) and Engram host offload (`9038b37`). The integration baseline is main `b8db6e985`, paired with vLLM `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Users can select the V4.1 model/frontend and configure Engram storage/offload. The tutorial and launch examples cover A3 deployment with DSpark and full decode graphs. Host offload adds a native CPU extension build dependency through the existing CMake build.

### How was this patch tested?

Added tests cover V4.1 cache allocation and metadata, compressor/indexer and attention operator contracts, model configuration, frontend encoding, DSpark, fresh-process imports, Engram storage/offload, and integration with the worker/model runner.

Earlier integration state `2ac02e6` with vLLM `a97dacb71` passed 400 framework unit tests, 3 fresh-process import cases, and 44 targeted regressions. An A3 single-node TP8/DP2/EP16 deployment with Engram disabled also exercised ordinary generation, thinking mode, and graph replay. These results predate the current main rebase and host-offload commit and are not claimed as full validation of this PR head.

Current-head CI and complete end-to-end/GPQA accuracy results remain to be confirmed. No passing two-node Engram or host-offload accuracy result is claimed here.
